keyFindings.description: Hides an error. The refresher writes `dispatch_url: dispatch.enabled ? dispatch.url : null`, but the hook compares it at :329 with sessionDispatchUrl, which is set without reading the token. So when the `!` token command fails (not signed in, exit 3), the refresher records null and the URLs never match. The hook drops the refresher's real error ('dispatch.token's command exited with status 3') and says 'the refresher read no Dispatch, not the Dispatch envoy.json names now', which is false. Both thermonuclear agents reproduced it with the committed dist. Fix: record the URL the refresher targeted, with the same function the hook uses (sessionDispatchUrl/dispatchUrl), so a matching URL carries the refresher's own text. Add a test with a token command that fails fast.

The timing checks flake on a loaded pod: the reviewer saw 2 of 3 full-file runs fail ('a quick one gives the bearer at once' at :338, and the new cross-URL test at :439, each because the refresher had not finished 800-833 ms after the hook started), and the tester saw 2 of 7 fail on `wallMs < 1000`. The claude-envoy job is not in the required set (lint, typecheck, test, pr-title). Since this round requests changes anyway, the request asks for the checks to assert the bounds the design states, not wall time from process start.
